Hi Caroline — thanks for the clear list. Quick summary up front: for EU B2B purchases with a validated German VAT ID we typically issue a net invoice and include the reverse-charge wording; we do a VIES lookup and we do not currently register for VAT in Germany. For India/GST it depends on the billed legal entity and place of supply — more details below.

Action items well take now:
- Finance (cc Neha) will run a VIES validation for the VAT ID you confirm and prepare an amended invoice if appropriate.
- Ill update the proforma to show net pricing and include the exact reverse-charge clause we will print on the final invoice.

Questions for you: please confirm the legal company name as registered on the VAT database and the exact VAT ID to validate (the one on the final PO needs to match). Also tell us which legal entity will sign the PO (GNEX GmbH or the India subsidiary).

Notes on India (short): if the recipient is an Indian business and GST rules deem the place of supply to be India, local GST (IGST) may apply. Redwood is a US-headquartered supplier and we are not currently registered for GST in India; that usually means the buyer accounts for reverse charge under their local rules. If you plan for Redwood to invoice a local India entity and need Redwood to collect GST, well need to discuss registration or work through a channel partner.

Ill attach a short guide we send customers on reverse-charge steps.

Thanks — Vivek

Hi Caroline — looping in finance to confirm exact language and next steps. Ive validated the VAT ID you provided against VIES and captured a screenshot (attached). Summary below and what well include on the invoice:

Summary (EU / Germany):
- VIES check: DE999999999 — VALID as of 2026-06-18 14:22 UTC. (see vat_validation_screenshot.png)
- As a US supplier without German VAT registration, Redwood will not charge German VAT on a B2B supply to a VAT-registered German business.
- Invoice will be net (no VAT). We will include the buyer VAT ID and the following statement: "Reverse charge — Article 194 of Council Directive 2006/112/EC. Tax liability rests with the recipient of the supply (buyer)."
- We will also include our US tax identification (EIN: 12-3456789) and the invoice number template. If your AP requires an explicit line stating that Redwood does not have German VAT registration, we can add: "Supplier not registered for VAT in Germany."

India / GST guidance (short):
- If Redwood invoices an Indian legal entity (GNEX India Pvt Ltd) for a service with place of supply in India, GST could apply. Redwood is not registered for GST in India; therefore, in most cases the Indian recipient would self-assess under reverse charge (IGST) unless Redwood elects to register or bills through an Indian reseller/partner.
- If you want Redwood to collect GST, we can scope registration or connect you with our local billing partner (adds ~2–4 weeks).
